findings.issue: StampEntry() unconditionally overwrites CreatedAt, UpdatedAt and forces RowVersion = 1 on every Added SyncedEntity, with no opt-out. The sync-import layer (ARCHITECTURE.md §6, work package B6) must insert incoming rows preserving the originating device's created_at/updated_at/row_version; through this context that is impossible — every imported row is restamped with local time and row_version 1, which destroys the base_version/row_version conflict detection §6 specifies. The author recognised exactly this case for OriginDevice ('only when the caller has not already set one') but applied the exemption to that one column only, so the XML doc's claim that 'tests and sync-import replay that set it explicitly are unaffected' is false for the other three columns.
findings.fix: In StampEntry's EntityState.Added branch, set CreatedAt/UpdatedAt only when they equal default(DateTime) and set RowVersion only when it is 0; or add an explicit `public IDisposable SuppressAuditStamps()` scope on WakeelDb (a bool field checked at the top of ApplySyncedEntityStamps/Async) for the import path. Add a test that adds a SyncedEntity with CreatedAt/UpdatedAt/RowVersion pre-set and asserts all three survive SaveChanges.

findings.issue: SaveChanges/SaveChangesAsync do not intercept EntityState.Deleted on a SyncedEntity, so `db.Correspondence.Remove(x); db.SaveChanges();` physically deletes an official row. DATA-MODEL.md §0 ('حذف منطقي فقط؛ لا حذف فعلي للسجلات الرسمية') and ARCHITECTURE.md §12 forbid this, and because 0001_initial.sql declares only AFTER INSERT/UPDATE change_log triggers the deletion is invisible to sync: the row is silently resurrected by the next import from another PC while local references dangle. Nothing in Core prevents or even warns about this, and the other packages (B3–B6) are written against this API.
findings.fix: In StampEntry, handle `case EntityState.Deleted:` by converting to a soft delete — `entry.State = EntityState.Modified; entry.Entity.DeletedAt = now; entry.Entity.UpdatedAt = now; entry.Entity.RowVersion += 1;` — or throw InvalidOperationException naming the entity type. Expose a `SoftDelete<T>(T entity)` helper on WakeelDb or QueryableExtensions and document it. Add a test asserting Remove+SaveChanges leaves the row present with deleted_at set and writes a 'U' change_log entry.

findings.issue: EnsureCurrentCycleAsync's current-cycle lookup uses IgnoreDeleted(), justified by the comment 'ux_financial_cycles_start_date is a partial unique index (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL) that still enforces uniqueness against a soft-deleted row'. That premise is wrong: a partial index omits rows failing its WHERE clause, so a soft-deleted row does not occupy the start_date at all (verified against Microsoft.Data.Sqlite — inserting a second row with the same start_date over a soft-deleted one succeeds). The real effect is a soft-delete leak: a logically deleted cycle is resurrected as 'the current cycle' and returned with DeletedAt still set and Status untouched, so callers attach transactions/cash counts/monthly reports to a cycle that the global query filter hides from every list and report. FinancialCycleTests.EnsureCurrentCycle_AfterSoftDeleteOfCurrentCycle_DoesNotThrow_AndReusesTheHiddenRow asserts the buggy behaviour and repeats the same incorrect claim (its 'before the fix this threw SQLite Error 19' assertion is untrue), so the test no longer guards anything real.
findings.fix: Remove IgnoreDeleted() from the lookup — the filtered query plus the partial index is already correct and creates a fresh Open cycle for the start date. If reuse of a hidden row is genuinely desired, keep IgnoreDeleted() but clear the row first (`current.DeletedAt = null; current.Status = FinancialCycleStatus.Open;`) before returning. Correct the comment in the service and in the test, and change the test to assert the returned cycle has DeletedAt == null and Status == Open.

findings.issue: Line 782: ux_assets_inventory_number was made partial (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL). Inventory numbers (`<office_code>-<seq>`, AGREEMENT item 45) must stay unique forever — the same reasoning this file itself gives two hundred lines earlier for deliberately leaving ux_correspondence_official_number unfiltered. A new asset can now reuse a soft-deleted asset's inventory number, which breaks custody history and collides on sync with a PC that still holds the old row.
findings.fix: Revert ux_assets_inventory_number to an unfiltered unique index and handle the 'a hidden row already owns this number' case in the asset service with an IgnoreDeleted() lookup, matching the correspondence policy.

findings.issue: Line 987: ux_monthly_reports_cycle_id is unfiltered while ux_financial_cycles_start_date and ux_assets_inventory_number were made partial — three unique indexes on soft-deleted tables now follow three different policies. As it stands a soft-deleted monthly_report permanently blocks creating a replacement report for that cycle, and B5's filtered lookup will not see the blocker, so the failure surfaces as an unmapped SQLite UNIQUE error rather than a handled case.
findings.fix: Choose one policy for all soft-deleted unique constraints (recommended: unfiltered index + IgnoreDeleted() lookups in the services) and state it once in a header comment in the SQL file.

findings.issue: ResolveLocalDeviceId/ResolveLocalDeviceIdAsync cache string.Empty permanently when `installation` has not been populated yet (`_localDeviceId = deviceId == Guid.Empty ? string.Empty : ...`). A WakeelDb lives for the whole run of the app, so if any synced row is written before the .wakeel-setup file is consumed, every synced row written afterwards on that context silently gets an empty origin_device — exactly the unattributed-row failure mode the round-1 fix was meant to eliminate, but now invisible because the column is non-empty-checked nowhere.
findings.fix: Only cache a non-empty result: `if (deviceId == Guid.Empty) return string.Empty;` (no assignment to _localDeviceId), then `return _localDeviceId = FormatDeviceId(deviceId);`. Add a test that writes a synced row before SeedInstallation, seeds it, writes a second row, and asserts the second row's origin_device is non-empty.

findings.issue: IssueCoreAsync reads official_numbers.last_seq, increments it in memory and saves with no optimistic-concurrency guard. Two WakeelDb instances over the same file (e.g. the app plus a background job, or a second DbSession opened as several tests do) can both read last_seq = N and both write N+1, issuing the same official number twice; only ux_correspondence_official_number would catch it, and then only once the correspondence row is written. ARCHITECTURE.md §5 calls the issue 'transactional'.
findings.fix: Mark the column as a concurrency token in OnModelCreating (`modelBuilder.Entity<OfficialNumber>().Property(e => e.LastSeq).IsConcurrencyToken()`) so a stale write throws DbUpdateConcurrencyException, or replace the read-modify-write with `UPDATE official_numbers SET last_seq = last_seq + 1 WHERE kind = @k AND year = @y AND last_seq = @old` and retry when 0 rows are affected.

findings.issue: Neither ComputeCycle nor EnsureCurrentCycleAsync normalizes the incoming DateTime's Kind — they use `referenceDate.Date` / `now.Date` directly, while ClockCheckService and OfficialNumberService both open with an explicit Utc/Local/Unspecified switch. A caller passing DateTime.Now shortly after local midnight (or shortly before, in a negative-offset zone) computes a cycle for the wrong day, and the mixed-Kind `c.EndDate < today` comparison is then translated to an ISO-text comparison against UTC-written values.
findings.fix: Add the same Kind normalization used in ClockCheckService.CheckAsync at the top of both methods and derive `today`/`date` from the normalized UTC value; add a test passing a Local-kind reference date near a cycle boundary.

findings.issue: Parse returns 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z for empty text and otherwise falls through to DateTime.Parse, which throws FormatException from inside EF materialization for unrecognised text. A corrupted or truncated NOT NULL timestamp therefore either reads back as year 1 — silently falling outside every ARCHITECTURE.md §6 date-range sync export and every attention-center window — or blows up mid-query with an exception ErrorMapper routes to the generic 'unexpected error' bucket. DateTimeConverterTests.Read_EmptyString_DoesNotThrow_AndYieldsUtcKind asserts only the Kind, so it pins the silent-year-1 behaviour as intended without anything detecting it.
findings.fix: Keep the tolerance but make it observable: wrap the fallback in try/catch, and have the caller-visible path record a health_snapshots entry (or at minimum an ILogger warning via the already-referenced Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions) naming the table and column, so a corrupted timestamp reaches the health center (W12) rather than disappearing.

findings.issue: Plural() renders count 0 with the broken-plural form ('0 مهام'). AGREEMENT item 53(c) requires deterministic templated Arabic with correct singular/dual/plural agreement; the natural rendering for the zero case in generated report sentences is 'لا مهام' or the 11+ tamyiz form. The author documented this as an explicit choice pending sign-off, but B5's report sentences will harden around whatever is chosen.
findings.fix: Get the supervisor's ruling, then either add a fifth `zero` parameter (defaulting to `plural` so existing call sites compile) or map 0 to pluralOver10; add the corresponding [InlineData(0, ...)] case to ArabicTextTests.

findings.issue: The class XML doc reads 'The على-disk layout of one الوكيل installation' — an Arabic word ('على') accidentally substituted for the English 'on' inside an English comment, presumably by an editor's autocorrect. ARCHITECTURE.md §12 requires code comments and XML docs in English.
findings.fix: Change to 'The on-disk layout of one الوكيل installation' (the intentional Arabic product name stays).

missing_spec_items: DATA-MODEL.md §1 annotates audit_log as synced read-only ('يُزامَن كقراءة فقط'), but it is implemented as a purely local table: no created_at/updated_at/origin_device/row_version/base_version/deleted_at columns and no change_log trigger. The SQL file documents the chosen resolution (B6 exports it by its own `at` range) as pending supervisor sign-off; it is still a deviation from the data model as written and needs an explicit ruling before B6 starts.

DATA-MODEL.md §3 document_pages and document_links carry no sync columns and no change_log triggers, so a synced `documents` row arrives on a second PC without its OCR page text or entity links (ARCHITECTURE.md §6 says every official table syncs). Documented in the SQL as 're-derived locally on the receiving device', which is a product decision, not a code one — needs sign-off.

ARCHITECTURE.md §5 requires the number to be issued 'داخل معاملة واحدة مع اعتماد المراسلة'. OfficialNumberService never opens a transaction itself; the contract is documented in the interface's XML doc and delegated entirely to the B3 caller, including the reload-after-rollback obligation. No Core-side helper (e.g. an IssueWithinAsync(Func<...>) or a transaction-required assertion) exists to make that contract hard to get wrong.

The 17 JSON columns are spelled without the _json suffix (cc, words, changes, fields, agenda, totals, overrides, asset_ids, counted, sections, readiness, filters, counts, ours, theirs, items, details), matching DATA-MODEL.md exactly — this is now consistent and correct, but it is listed here because the builder flagged it as needing a supervisor ruling (the alternative was amending DATA-MODEL.md to the _json spelling). No code change is needed if DATA-MODEL.md stands as written.

change_log UPDATE triggers now record the EDITING device (COALESCE((SELECT device_id FROM installation LIMIT 1), NEW.origin_device)) rather than the row's originating device. DATA-MODEL.md §11 does not define `change_log.device` semantics, and ARCHITECTURE.md §6's conflict model does not depend on it either way. The current choice is the useful one for a date-range export, but it should be written into DATA-MODEL.md §11 so B6 can rely on it.

Failed: 0, Passed: 144, Skipped: 0, Total: 144, 20s. No files were modified. One throwaway console project was created under the session scratchpad (not the repo) to verify the SQLite partial-index behaviour behind finding #3.

WHAT I VERIFIED AS CORRECT
- Schema/EF-model match: 66 CREATE TABLE statements vs exactly 66 DbSets; SchemaTests.EveryDbSet_IsQueryable materializes each one, so any column-name mismatch would fail — real coverage, not a tautology. I diffed every DATA-MODEL.md §1–§12 table's column list against 0001_initial.sql by script: every documented column is present, including the report_include/report_highlight/report_comment triples that DATA-MODEL abbreviates as "تقرير…".
- 44 synced tables, each with exactly one AFTER INSERT and one AFTER UPDATE change_log trigger (plus the 3 search_fts sync triggers) — count matches the 44 SyncedEntity subclasses one-for-one; every synced table has the full §0 column set.
- snake_case naming convention round-trips the awkward identifiers correctly (OrgX25519Pub -> org_x25519_pub, Sha256 -> sha256, ExecutionPct -> execution_pct); enum snake_case matches DATA-MODEL's literal tokens (top_secret, not_started, in_service, transfer_out, awaiting_issue, phone_qr, bonus_rule, late_tasks, derived_print).
- SQLCipher: Batteries_V2.Init() once via Interlocked; Pooling=false (correct and well-reasoned — a pooled handle would defeat wrong-key validation); key length checked; sqlite_master probe makes a wrong key fail inside Open(); WAL/foreign_keys/busy_timeout applied after keying. The `PRAGMA key = "x'<hex>'"` interpolation is the documented SQLCipher form and the interpolated value is hex from a byte[], so it is not an injection surface. Every other raw SQL statement in src and tests uses parameters. The heap-residency of the key string is unavoidable with Microsoft.Data.Sqlite and is documented accurately.
- Migration safety: each script applies inside its own transaction with its schema_versions row; the newer-database guard throws before applying anything; GetCurrentVersion is a genuinely pure read. Both are covered by real tests.
- Numbering: the ARCHITECTURE §5 example reproduces exactly (20260911/12001); yearly reset, independent in/out sequences, 900 warning, 999 exhaustion and the cross-year backdating watermark are all covered by tests that assert behaviour rather than restate the implementation. The Format() replacement order (YYYYMMDD, then SSS, then D, then E) is safe because the longer tokens are consumed first.
- Cycle math is right for every case in AGREEMENT item 52 including the 20/09→19/10 example, start day 1, leap and non-leap February, and the year-end crossing.
- ErrorMapper's "no Latin letters / no digits" tests are genuine regex assertions over all five buckets, and the DbUpdateException-unwrapping tests exercise the real EF wrapping shape.

TEST-QUALITY CAVEAT
Almost all 144 tests assert real behaviour. The one exception is FinancialCycleTests.EnsureCurrentCycle_AfterSoftDeleteOfCurrentCycle_DoesNotThrow_AndReusesTheHiddenRow (finding #3): its premise — that the insert previously threw SQLite Error 19 — is false, so the test would pass with or without the change it claims to guard, and it pins a soft-delete leak in place. NumberingTests.Issue_EarlierDateThanLastIssued_IsRefused is slightly imprecise too: with the two-arg overload the throw can come from the clock check rather than the date watermark, so it does not isolate what its name says (the cross-year test does, via the explicit-verdict overload).

API SHAPE FOR OTHER PACKAGES
AddWakeelCore's split — singletons for IClock/IIdGenerator/IErrorMapper, scoped for the db-backed services, WakeelDb left to the host because the key only exists after unlock — is the right shape for ARCHITECTURE.md §10's scoped-service model, and ServiceRegistrationTests resolves all eight. The two blockers for downstream packages are findings #1 and #2: B6 cannot import rows through this context without losing their audit columns, and B3–B5 have no soft-delete path (and no guard against the hard-delete that the data model forbids). Both are small, local fixes in WakeelDb.StampEntry.

Verdict is 'fix' solely because of the three medium findings; build and tests are green and the package is otherwise complete and well-documented.
